column1: # The fixes a release must carry. `just release-build` runs tools/release/carry.sh over this file before it
# touches the box, and refuses a commit that lacks any row, so a candidate is never cut while a fix it needs
# sits on a branch.
# One row a fix, three tab-separated columns:  commit<TAB>name<TAB>why
#   commit  a hash on main (12 hex digits or the full 40; a shorter one can turn ambiguous as the repository grows),
#           that must be an ancestor of the commit being released; or the
#           word `pending` for a fix known and not landed yet, which refuses every release until its row holds
#           a hash.
#   name    one word: the round or the fix.
#   why     one line: what the release is wrong without.
# Lines that start with `#` and empty lines are ignored. Any other line that is not three columns, with a
# commit that is neither a hash nor `pending`, or with an empty name or why, is refused with its line number.
# A row is added when a correctness fix lands (its hash), and when one is known and not yet landed (`pending`,
# replaced by its hash at landing). Rows stay after the release that needed them: a landed fix stays an
# ancestor. The lead rewrites a row's hash when a rebase moves the commit, before landing.
